# bushfireheat

bushfireheat helps risk analysts who price bushfire exposure in
south-eastern Australia answer one question: **how much more often does
extreme heat occur in the fire season now than in 1950–1979, and does
the answer depend on where the threshold for “extreme” is set?**

The package contains daily fire-season weather for eight towns affected
by the 2019/20 Black Summer fires, functions that count hot days and
compare periods, and a Shiny app for exploring the change town by town.

Documentation website:
<https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-hanwen-l/>

## Installation

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("ETC5523-2026/etc5523-assignment-4-hanwen-l")
```

## Launch the app

``` r

library(bushfireheat)
run_app()
```

## Use the functions

``` r

seasons <- summarise_seasons(fire_daily, threshold = 35)
compare_periods(seasons)
plot_hot_days(seasons)
```

## Data

`fire_daily` holds the daily maximum temperature and rainfall for every
day of every September–February fire season from 1950/51 to 2025/26, and
`fire_towns` lists the towns. The values come from the ERA5 reanalysis
(Hersbach et al. 2023, <https://doi.org/10.24381/cds.adbb2d47>),
retrieved through the [Open-Meteo Historical Weather
API](https://open-meteo.com/) under the [CC BY
4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) licence. Generated
using Copernicus Climate Change Service information. The daily values
were subset to fire-season months; no other changes were made.

[`data-raw/fire_daily.R`](https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-hanwen-l/data-raw/fire_daily.R)
downloads and prepares the data. Raw downloads are cached in
`data-raw/raw/`, so the script rebuilds the package data without calling
the API again.

## Generative AI declaration

Generative AI declaration: I used Claude (Claude Code, Anthropic) to
explain the assignment requirements, compare candidate data sources and
test the Open-Meteo API, and to draft the initial package structure: the
data-preparation script, the exported functions with their documentation
and tests, a starter Shiny app, this README and the vignette. I checked
and revised all generated code and text.

# Package index

## Data

- [`fire_daily`](https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-hanwen-l/reference/fire_daily.md)
  : Daily fire-season weather for towns in south-eastern Australia
- [`fire_towns`](https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-hanwen-l/reference/fire_towns.md)
  : Towns covered by bushfireheat

## Count and compare hot days

- [`summarise_seasons()`](https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-hanwen-l/reference/summarise_seasons.md)
  : Count hot days in each fire season
- [`compare_periods()`](https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-hanwen-l/reference/compare_periods.md)
  : Compare hot days and rainfall between two periods
- [`plot_hot_days()`](https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-hanwen-l/reference/plot_hot_days.md)
  : Plot hot days per fire season

## App

- [`run_app()`](https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-hanwen-l/reference/run_app.md)
  : Launch the fire-season heat explorer
